title: Most international goals in men's football, all time
hook: Who has scored the most goals for his country?

source.name: Wikipedia per-player international goal lists, selected from the 50+ goals list (MediaWiki API)
source.terms: Wikipedia text is CC BY-SA 4.0; this derived data must credit Wikipedia contributors and carry the same licence.
source.notes: Entities: the 20 players at or above the 20th-highest total (72 goals) in the 50+ list, plus the record holders named in its History section (Imre Schlosser, Ferenc Puskás, Mokhtar Dahari, Ali Daei, Cristiano Ronaldo). Vivian Woodward is named there only conditionally ("would make him the first..."; his total counts England amateur matches) and is not treated as a holder. Each series is counted goal by goal from the player's dated goal table at its revid (see perEntity). Goals before 1950 are carried into the 1950 value; the series stops at 2025-12-31, so players still active show fewer goals than their current totals. Excluded (no per-goal data, not interpolated): Vivian Woodward: contested total (75): the 50+ list counts England amateur matches for him and its History section names him only conditionally; footnote: "Vivian Woodward scored 29 goals in 23 matches for the professional England team between 1903 and 1911, and 46 goals in 30 matches for the England amateur side between 1906 and 1914; all matches for the Amateur side were considered official internationals for their respective opponents.". Mismatches against the 50+ list's current totals (built from goal table minus list): Imre Schlosser 58 vs 59 (-1). Left as the goal tables give them.

events.text: Imre Schlosser holds the record entering 1950: 58 goals
Ferenc Puskás passes Imre Schlosser for the all-time record: 59 goals
Ferenc Puskás becomes the first of these players to 75 international goals
Mokhtar Dahari passes Ferenc Puskás for the all-time record: 85 goals
Ali Daei passes Mokhtar Dahari for the all-time record: 90 goals
Ali Daei becomes the first of these players to 100 international goals
Cristiano Ronaldo passes Ali Daei for the all-time record: 109 goals
Cristiano Ronaldo becomes the first of these players to 125 international goals
